quests.hint: This noun refers to the process of supervising activities to ensure rules are being followed.
quests.explanation: 'Regulatory oversight,' 'parliamentary oversight,' and 'lack of oversight' are key. 'Oversight' can also mean a careless mistake: 'an unfortunate oversight.' Context determines meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: The new law strengthens independent ___ of the financial services industry.
quests.correctAnswer: The new law strengthens independent oversight of the financial services industry.

quests.hint: This noun refers to an official instruction, authority, or task given to someone.
quests.explanation: 'Electoral mandate,' 'clear mandate,' and 'act beyond your mandate' are key. 'Mandate' is also a verb: 'mandated by law.' 'Mandatory' means required by law or rule.
quests.textToSpeak: The government claimed it had a clear ___ from voters to implement the full reform programme.
quests.correctAnswer: The government claimed it had a clear mandate from voters to implement the full reform programme.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the defined area of responsibility, authority, or scope for a role or body.
quests.explanation: 'Within the remit of,' 'beyond my remit,' and 'core remit' are key. If something is 'outside your remit,' it is not your responsibility to deal with it.
quests.textToSpeak: Negotiating international treaties falls entirely within the Foreign Office's ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Negotiating international treaties falls entirely within the Foreign Office's remit.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the right or condition of self-governance - making your own decisions.
quests.explanation: 'Academic autonomy,' 'regional autonomy,' and 'respect autonomy' are key. 'Autonomous' is the adjective. 'Autonomy' in healthcare means the patient's right to make their own decisions.
quests.textToSpeak: The proposal would give schools greater ___ to design their own curriculum.
quests.correctAnswer: The proposal would give schools greater autonomy to design their own curriculum.

quests.hint: This noun refers to formal disagreement with an official decision or majority view.
quests.explanation: 'Voice dissent,' 'political dissent,' and 'dissenting opinion' are key. 'Dissenter' is the person. A 'dissenting judge' writes an opinion disagreeing with the court's majority decision.
quests.textToSpeak: Three senior ministers recorded their ___ from the cabinet's decision in the official minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: Three senior ministers recorded their dissent from the cabinet's decision in the official minutes.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a formal process of resolving disputes through an independent third party.
quests.explanation: 'Binding arbitration,' 'submit to arbitration,' and 'arbitration panel' are key. 'Arbitrate' is the verb. 'Arbitrator' is the neutral decision-maker. Less formal and cheaper than court proceedings.
quests.textToSpeak: The employment dispute was referred to independent ___ to avoid a lengthy court battle.
quests.correctAnswer: The employment dispute was referred to independent arbitration to avoid a lengthy court battle.

quests.hint: This noun refers to strict honesty and strong moral principles in professional conduct.
quests.explanation: 'Act with probity,' 'financial probity,' and 'a person of probity' are key. More formal than 'integrity.' Used especially in public office, financial, and legal contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: Public officials are expected to conduct themselves with absolute ___ at all times.
quests.correctAnswer: Public officials are expected to conduct themselves with absolute probity at all times.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the use of threats or force to make someone do something against their will.
quests.explanation: 'Under coercion,' 'economic coercion,' and 'coercive tactics' are key. 'Coerce' is the verb: 'coerced into signing.' A contract signed under coercion may be legally void.
quests.textToSpeak: She claimed she had signed the agreement under ___ and against her own free will.
quests.correctAnswer: She claimed she had signed the agreement under coercion and against her own free will.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a force or impulse that causes a process to develop or happen more quickly.
quests.explanation: 'Provide the impetus,' 'give impetus to,' and 'the impetus for change' are key. 'Impetus' is uncountable in this sense. 'Act as an impetus' means to trigger movement or action.
quests.textToSpeak: The financial crisis gave fresh ___ to the push for tighter banking regulation.
quests.correctAnswer: The financial crisis gave fresh impetus to the push for tighter banking regulation.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a standard or measure used to evaluate or track performance.
quests.explanation: 'Key metric,' 'performance metric,' and 'measure by this metric' are key. 'Metrics' (plural) are the measurable indicators used to track progress. 'Vanity metrics' look good but mean little.
quests.textToSpeak: The company uses several key ___ to measure the success of its marketing campaigns.
quests.correctAnswer: The company uses several key metrics to measure the success of its marketing campaigns.

quests.hint: This adjective describes a statement or situation that could be interpreted in more than one way.
quests.explanation: 'Deliberately equivocal,' 'an equivocal answer,' and 'his response was equivocal' are key. 'Equivocate' is the verb meaning to speak in a deliberately vague and uncommitted way.
quests.textToSpeak: The minister gave an ___ response that satisfied neither side of the debate.
quests.correctAnswer: The minister gave an equivocal response that satisfied neither side of the debate.

quests.hint: This verb means to confirm or give additional support to an existing claim or account.
quests.explanation: 'Corroborate a story,' 'corroborating evidence,' and 'independently corroborated' are key. 'Corroboration' is the noun. 'Corroborating witness' is one who supports the main account.
quests.textToSpeak: The second witness completely ___ the timeline given by the first person who testified.
quests.correctAnswer: The second witness completely corroborated the timeline given by the first person who testified.

quests.hint: This verb means to make a bad situation less severe or painful.
quests.explanation: 'Ameliorate suffering,' 'ameliorate conditions,' and 'difficult to ameliorate' are key. 'Amelioration' is the noun. More formal than 'improve' or 'alleviate.' Used in academic and official writing.
quests.textToSpeak: The new funding package was designed to ___ the worst effects of the housing shortage.
quests.correctAnswer: The new funding package was designed to ameliorate the worst effects of the housing shortage.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that continues without stopping or changing.
quests.explanation: 'Perpetual motion,' 'perpetual state of,' and 'in perpetuity' (forever) are key. 'Perpetually' is the adverb. 'Perpetuate' is the related verb meaning to cause something to continue.
quests.textToSpeak: The organization has been in a ___ state of crisis since the leadership scandal broke.
quests.correctAnswer: The organization has been in a perpetual state of crisis since the leadership scandal broke.

quests.hint: This adjective describes language, customs, or laws that are very old and no longer relevant.
quests.explanation: 'Archaic language,' 'archaic law,' and 'archaic custom' are key. 'Archaic' is stronger than 'old-fashioned.' In linguistics, 'archaic vocabulary' refers to words no longer in common use.
quests.textToSpeak: Several ___ provisions in the legislation date back over two hundred years and need reform.
quests.correctAnswer: Several archaic provisions in the legislation date back over two hundred years and need reform.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the breaking of something into smaller, disconnected parts.
quests.explanation: 'Social fragmentation,' 'political fragmentation,' and 'fragmentation of services' are key. 'Fragment' is the noun (a small piece) or verb (to break apart). 'Defragmentation' means bringing back together.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ of the opposition vote allowed the ruling party to win with a small share.
quests.correctAnswer: The fragmentation of the opposition vote allowed the ruling party to win with a small share.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the quality of sticking together as a unified and connected whole.
quests.explanation: 'Social cohesion,' 'team cohesion,' and 'lack of cohesion' are key. 'Cohesive' is the adjective: 'a cohesive team.' 'Cohesion' in a written text means how well ideas connect.
quests.textToSpeak: Strong community ___ is essential for managing the social impacts of rapid change.
quests.correctAnswer: Strong community cohesion is essential for managing the social impacts of rapid change.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a system for classifying things into ordered groups or categories.
quests.explanation: 'Biological taxonomy,' 'develop a taxonomy,' and 'a taxonomy of skills' are key. 'Taxonomic' is the adjective. Bloom's Taxonomy classifies levels of educational learning objectives.
quests.textToSpeak: The researcher developed a comprehensive ___ of errors commonly made by language learners.
quests.correctAnswer: The researcher developed a comprehensive taxonomy of errors commonly made by language learners.

quests.hint: This verb means to describe the exact boundary, scope, or outline of something precisely.
quests.explanation: 'Delineate responsibilities,' 'clearly delineated,' and 'delineate the scope' are key. 'Delineation' is the noun. Used in law, geography, and organizational management.
quests.textToSpeak: The contract carefully ___ the responsibilities of each party to avoid future disputes.
quests.correctAnswer: The contract carefully delineates the responsibilities of each party to avoid future disputes.

quests.hint: This verb means to draw out or provoke a particular response, emotion, or piece of information.
quests.explanation: 'Elicit a response,' 'elicit information,' and 'elicit emotion' are key. 'Elicitation' is the noun. A key skill in teaching: 'elicit from students rather than simply telling them.'
quests.textToSpeak: A good interviewer knows how to ___ honest and detailed answers through careful questioning.
quests.correctAnswer: A good interviewer knows how to elicit honest and detailed answers through careful questioning.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a right or privilege belonging to a particular person or role.
quests.explanation: 'Your prerogative,' 'executive prerogative,' and 'royal prerogative' are key. 'That is your prerogative' means it is your right to decide. 'Prerogative powers' are unilateral government powers.
quests.textToSpeak: It is entirely the CEO's ___ to appoint whomever she sees fit for the senior role.
quests.correctAnswer: It is entirely the CEO's prerogative to appoint whomever she sees fit for the senior role.

quests.hint: This adjective describes the person currently holding a particular position or office.
quests.explanation: 'Incumbent president,' 'the incumbent,' and 'incumbent government' are key. 'Incumbent' also means obligatory: 'it is incumbent upon us to act.' Both meanings are common.
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ prime minister was widely expected to lose the election by a significant margin.
quests.correctAnswer: The incumbent prime minister was widely expected to lose the election by a significant margin.

quests.hint: This verb means to make a law, decision, or announcement known publicly and officially.
quests.explanation: 'Promulgate a law,' 'promulgate regulations,' and 'widely promulgated' are key. 'Promulgation' is the noun. Similar to 'publish' or 'announce' but implies formal official dissemination.
quests.textToSpeak: The new regulations were ___ by the Ministry of Health and came into force immediately.
quests.correctAnswer: The new regulations were promulgated by the Ministry of Health and came into force immediately.

quests.hint: This verb means to arrange rules, principles, or laws into a clear and systematic written code.
quests.explanation: 'Codify laws,' 'codify practices,' and 'codification of' are key. 'Code' (a set of laws) is related. 'Codified constitution' means one written down in a single document.
quests.textToSpeak: The task force was asked to ___ the existing unwritten conventions into a formal charter.
quests.correctAnswer: The task force was asked to codify the existing unwritten conventions into a formal charter.

quests.hint: This verb means to restrict, limit, or hold back the development of something.
quests.explanation: 'Constrain growth,' 'constrain behaviour,' and 'tightly constrained' are key. 'Constraint' is the noun. 'Within the constraints of' means working within a set of limits.
quests.textToSpeak: Limited resources ___ the government's ability to respond quickly to the growing crisis.
quests.correctAnswer: Limited resources constrain the government's ability to respond quickly to the growing crisis.

quests.hint: This verb means to make an official judgment or decision in a dispute or competition.
quests.explanation: 'Adjudicate a dispute,' 'adjudicate on,' and 'adjudicating panel' are key. 'Adjudication' is the noun. 'Adjudicator' is the person. More formal than 'judge' in many contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: An independent panel was appointed to ___ on the contract dispute between the two firms.
quests.correctAnswer: An independent panel was appointed to adjudicate on the contract dispute between the two firms.

quests.hint: This verb means to prevent something from happening, or to make it impossible.
quests.explanation: 'Preclude the possibility,' 'preclude someone from,' and 'not preclude' are key. 'Preclusion' is the noun. 'That does not preclude' means that possibility still exists.
quests.textToSpeak: His previous conviction did not automatically ___ him from applying for the position.
quests.correctAnswer: His previous conviction did not automatically preclude him from applying for the position.

quests.hint: This verb means to specify a requirement or condition that must be included in an agreement.
quests.explanation: 'Stipulate conditions,' 'the contract stipulates,' and 'as stipulated' are key. 'Stipulation' is the noun. What is 'stipulated' is mandatory - it must happen or be included.
quests.textToSpeak: The grant agreement ___ that all findings must be made publicly available within two years.
quests.correctAnswer: The grant agreement stipulates that all findings must be made publicly available within two years.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially declare that someone is not guilty or not responsible for something.
quests.explanation: 'Exonerate a suspect,' 'fully exonerated,' and 'exoneration' are key. 'Exonerate' is stronger than 'acquit' - it clears not just of legal guilt but of moral blame too.
quests.textToSpeak: New DNA evidence ___ the man who had spent twelve years in prison for the crime.
quests.correctAnswer: New DNA evidence exonerated the man who had spent twelve years in prison for the crime.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially make something into law or a binding rule.
quests.explanation: 'Enact legislation,' 'enact a policy,' and 'enacted by parliament' are key. 'Enactment' is the noun. 'Re-enact' means to perform something again. 'Act' (noun) is what has been enacted.
quests.textToSpeak: Parliament voted to ___ the new legislation on data protection by a large majority.
quests.correctAnswer: Parliament voted to enact the new legislation on data protection by a large majority.
